title: Measuring the Window Before a Change of Model on Equipment Rental and Demo Kit
content:
Where the shop's own records show how long the rider has actually been on the kit, that is the better measure of how long they took to ask for a change than the dates on the paperwork.

## The rule

Where the rental account carries at least one date the kit was out on the agreement, the window is the count of the dates the account shows the kit out, less one.

Where the rental account carries no date the kit was out on the agreement, and the agreement stands with kit set aside and not yet collected, the window is nil.

In any other case nothing under this heading changes how the window is measured.

## The two conditions in combination

| Dates the account carries for the kit being out | The agreement stands with kit set aside and not yet collected | The window |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 or more | either way | the count of those dates, less one |
| none | yes | nil |
| none | no | nothing under this heading changes it |

The first row governs wherever any date out stands on the account, whatever the agreement's standing. The second is reached only where no such date stands at all.

## Worked counts on a hypothetical agreement

Take an Equipment Rental and Demo agreement recorded on the 2nd of January on which a change of model was raised on the 9th.

- The account carries 5 dates the kit was out: the window is 4 days.
- The account carries 1 date the kit was out: the window is nil, one date less one being nothing.
- The account carries no date the kit was out and the agreement stands with kit set aside and not yet collected: the window is nil.
- The account carries no date the kit was out and the agreement stands reserved: nothing under this heading changes how the window is measured.

The window is never taken below zero.

## Point of judgement

**Dates out rather than days on the paper.** Where the account carries dates the kit was out, it is those dates that are counted, and the dates the reservation was written across do not come into it.
